WS5 [R-FCAL-01 amended]: the walk-forward becomes an ACTUATOR. engine/walkforward/decision_rule.py is pre-registered and mechanical — a bias is corrected only if it is robust across bootstrap blocks {2,3,4}, its sign holds in every era with at least five cells, and the driver BEATS FREEZE out of sample; the strength is the reliability weight b*max(0,1-se^2/b^2) on the bias's own standard error, which retires the typed half-strength default. Run on all five records: 9 adopt, 37 watch, 42 none out of 88 drivers. It correctly DECLINES PHDC's +1.12 profit bias — the largest number this project has measured about its own method — because that driver loses to 'no change' at skill -1.87, and correcting a bias in a forecast worse than no change is polishing the wrong object. scripts/check_walkforward_actuation.py checks three things from outside: the log reconciles to what the rule adopts, forward drivers sit inside their own p10-p90 or are named and priced, and a crash is never silent. Twelve-case negative control. Four runs seeded on the ratchet because they ran under the PREVIOUS rule; AMOC conforms today.

Then engine/macro_history.py + engine/macro_history/EG.json: the point-in-time archive's SCHEMA and rule, committed with no figures, so every figure added later arrives under a standard rather than setting one. It REFUSES on a bare value, a partial vintage, an absent year and an unregistered tier — verified on all four — because an interpolated vintage corrupts the very error it is scored on and does so invisibly.
